redRegressions.before: New trust did not reserve future revocation capacity; a 4097th revocation made the store unreadable; coercible scalar types were accepted.
redRegressions.after: Admission reserves a revocation slot per active identity, full history rejects before mutation, and revocation JSON has strict scalar types.

redRegressions.before: Separate instances could pass the same key-ID or 32-active-key admission checks concurrently.
redRegressions.after: A directory-scoped JVM and OS lock protects complete reads/additions/revocations across instances.
redRegressions.fixture: The atomic-write seam delayed the first write deterministically before the directory-lock fix.

redRegressions.finding: Disabling general Jackson scalar coercion did not reject numeric reason-to-string conversion.
redRegressions.resolution: Explicit Textual coercion rules reject integer, float and boolean values; the targeted follow-up and both full builds passed.

failureMatrix: Concurrent attempts to bind one key ID preserve the first committed key and reject different material.
Concurrent additions at 31 active keys admit exactly one new key.
An add that fails before commit can retry; an uncertain add after commit returns the same key on retry.
Revocation write failure before commit preserves the active key.
Committed revocation takes effect while the stale public key remains; retry preserves original bytes, reason and time and finishes cleanup.
OS file lock is held during injected write callbacks and released after exceptions.
4095 retired identities plus one active key deny a new key and retain the reserved final revocation slot.
Legacy full history with an active key rejects further revocation before creating an unreadable entry.
Another store instance revoking a publisher invalidates load/list/repeated install without changing the imported bytes.

signerArtifact: Both JVMs checked the final Java 25 shaded artifact targeting release 21 using ephemeral test keys.
limitations: Publisher fault injection uses an atomic-write callback; successful commits use the actual file writer. It is not storage-device failure testing.
Concurrency evidence covers multiple instances in one JVM and checks OS-lock ownership. No new publisher multi-process or network-filesystem claim.
All trust operations now require access to the writable .publisher.lock file.

Legacy histories already at 4096 revoked identities can remain readable with active keys, but further revocation rejects before writing. Capacity migration preserving permanent revocations remains operational work.
No publisher IDs, old signatures, valid schema-v1 data or private imported bytes are rewritten automatically.
No new Paper/Folia client, operator trust-root, real third-party bridge, human acceptance or official signing evidence.
P0-P11 goal remains active; external phase gates remain incomplete.
